source: IC-7300 Full Manual rev. 11 (IC-7300_ENG_FM_11), section 19 command table and data formats; items 0196-0216 also in the firmware Information sheets V1.30 / V1.40. Formats checked by reading the factory defaults on firmware 1.42.

items.name: SSB RX HPF/LPF
items.note: two bytes: HPF (00 = through, 01-20 = 100-2000 Hz), LPF (05-24 = 500-2400 Hz, 25 = through) (p. 19-9); read-only here until the pair is edited as one

items.name: AM RX HPF/LPF
items.note: two bytes: HPF (00 = through, 01-20 = 100-2000 Hz), LPF (05-24 = 500-2400 Hz, 25 = through) (p. 19-9); read-only here until the pair is edited as one

items.name: FM RX HPF/LPF
items.note: two bytes: HPF (00 = through, 01-20 = 100-2000 Hz), LPF (05-24 = 500-2400 Hz, 25 = through) (p. 19-9); read-only here until the pair is edited as one

items.name: CW RX HPF/LPF
items.note: two bytes: HPF (00 = through, 01-20 = 100-2000 Hz), LPF (05-24 = 500-2400 Hz, 25 = through) (p. 19-9); read-only here until the pair is edited as one

items.name: RTTY RX HPF/LPF
items.note: two bytes: HPF (00 = through, 01-20 = 100-2000 Hz), LPF (05-24 = 500-2400 Hz, 25 = through) (p. 19-9); read-only here until the pair is edited as one

items.name: SSB TBW (WIDE)
items.note: one byte: high digit = higher edge (2500/2700/2800/2900 Hz), low digit = lower edge (100/200/300/500 Hz) (p. 19-9); the defaults read 30 / 12 / 03 / 12 on firmware 1.42

items.name: SSB TBW (MID)
items.note: one byte: high digit = higher edge (2500/2700/2800/2900 Hz), low digit = lower edge (100/200/300/500 Hz) (p. 19-9); the defaults read 30 / 12 / 03 / 12 on firmware 1.42

items.name: SSB TBW (NAR)
items.note: one byte: high digit = higher edge (2500/2700/2800/2900 Hz), low digit = lower edge (100/200/300/500 Hz) (p. 19-9); the defaults read 30 / 12 / 03 / 12 on firmware 1.42

items.name: SSB-D TBW
items.note: one byte: high digit = higher edge (2500/2700/2800/2900 Hz), low digit = lower edge (100/200/300/500 Hz) (p. 19-9); the defaults read 30 / 12 / 03 / 12 on firmware 1.42

items.name: TX Delay (70M)
items.note: 70 MHz is on some versions only; an IC-7300 without the 70 MHz band (firmware 1.42) answers NG

items.name: FM SPLIT Offset (HF)
items.note: 3 BCD bytes, least significant first, then 00 = + / 01 = - (p. 19-10)

items.name: FM SPLIT Offset (50M)
items.note: 3 BCD bytes, least significant first, then 00 = + / 01 = - (p. 19-10)

items.name: REF Adjust
items.note: the reference oscillator: this radio's own calibration, so a restore leaves it alone

items.name: [UP]
items.note: codes from the V1.40 Information sheet (p. 9); the full manual rev. 11 p. 19-12 prints 09 as BAND DOWN and stops at 18

items.name: [DN]
items.note: codes from the V1.40 Information sheet (p. 9); the full manual rev. 11 p. 19-12 prints 09 as BAND DOWN and stops at 18

items.name: ACC/USB AF SQL
items.note: rigs/IC-7300.rig names 1A 05 0061 'CI-V Output (ANT)': that is 0073

items.name: USB MOD Level
items.note: wfweb's MIC slider sets this one on a USB-connected IC-7300

items.name: CI-V Transceive
items.note: changing it can cut wfweb's own CI-V link to the radio

items.name: CI-V USB→REMOTE Transceive Address
items.note: the address in decimal BCD: 0000 = 00h to 0223 = DFh

items.name: CI-V USB Port
items.note: read only over CI-V (p. 19-5)

items.name: CI-V USB Echo Back
items.note: changing it can cut wfweb's own CI-V link to the radio

items.name: USB Serial Function
items.note: RTTY Decode takes the USB serial port away from CI-V: changing it can cut wfweb's own CI-V link to the radio

items.name: USB SEND
items.note: a USB control line that keys the radio; wfweb's serial port drives DTR/RTS, so this is read-only here

items.name: USB Keying (CW)
items.note: a USB control line that keys the radio; wfweb's serial port drives DTR/RTS, so this is read-only here

items.name: USB Keying (RTTY)
items.note: a USB control line that keys the radio; wfweb's serial port drives DTR/RTS, so this is read-only here

items.name: My Call (opening message text)
items.note: up to 10 characters, ASCII (p. 19-10)

items.name: Date
items.note: the clock: a restore leaves it alone

items.name: Time
items.note: the clock: a restore leaves it alone

items.name: Max Hold
items.note: the command table says 00-02 but lists only OFF / ON; the codes follow the Set screen (OFF, 10s Hold, ON), and the default (10s Hold) reads 01 on firmware 1.42
